title: Add CI workflow for release/* branches (stricter gates + deterministic builds + staged artifact publishing)
creator: Connor O'Brien
description:
We need a separate CI path for release branches (release/* and runtime-*-lts) that is stricter than mainline, optimized for stability and auditability.

This ticket covers:
1) CI workflows that automatically run on release branches and enforce additional gates (incl. deterministic builds).
2) A staged artifact publishing flow ("staging" publish for RCs + manual promote step for final release).
3) Documentation for release managers + runtime engineers on how to interpret failures/waivers.

Motivation (LTS): Dedicated/Private customers will pin to LTS patches and expect (a) reproducible artifacts tied to commits, (b) lower regression risk, and (c) a clear audit trail for what shipped.

Scope
- Triggers:
  - On push + PR targeting: release/*, runtime-*-lts
  - Nightly cron on release branches for drift detection (toolchain + dependency changes)
- Required checks (release branch only):
  - Deterministic build job (container + runtime binary/image):
    - Pin toolchain versions (compiler, CUDA base image, Python, buildkit)
    - Disable non-deterministic caching in the critical path (or make it content-addressable)
    - Produce build manifest: git SHA, submodule SHAs (if any), base image digest, build args
    - Rebuild twice and assert identical artifact digests (or fail with diff report)
  - Test suite:
    - Unit + integration tests (same as main)
    - Release-branch-only smoke tests (scheduler backpressure/overload scenarios; hooks to ENG-4831)
    - Upgrade/rollback sanity: ensure runtime image tags and manifests match expected semver scheme
  - Security/compliance hooks (for release branches):
    - Generate checksums and provenance metadata for artifacts (ties into ENG-4832)
    - SBOM generation job can be allowed as "non-blocking" initially, but must be emitted when available
  - Performance gate integration (blocking only when perf-canary summary is attached):
    - Pull perf-canary summary artifact for the candidate SHA and attach to the PR as a build artifact
    - Do not attempt to run full perf in this workflow (runner capacity is handled in perf-canary repo)
- Artifact staging and promotion:
  - For every successful release-branch build, publish artifacts to a staging location with restricted access:
    - runtime images tagged with -rc.N (or +build metadata) under a staging registry namespace
    - attach checksums + provenance JSON as CI artifacts, and publish to staging bucket
  - Manual approval step to promote staged artifacts to production tags (e.g., 1.18.1-lts):
    - restricted to Release Eng group (Connor + backups)
    - promotion step must verify digests match the staged build exactly

Non-goals
- Running the full perf suite inside the main runtime repo CI; perf-canary remains the source of truth.
- Adding new test coverage beyond targeted release-branch smoke tests; additional tests tracked elsewhere.

Open questions
- Whether to require SBOM as blocking for the first GA patch or allow it as best-effort until toolchain stabilizes.
- How strict to be on deterministic builds for GPU-kernel compilation artifacts (we may need exceptions for non-deterministic kernel autotune caches; prefer disabling on LTS).

Acceptance criteria
- A release-branch CI workflow exists and is enforced as required checks on release/* and runtime-*-lts branches.
- Deterministic build job produces: (a) manifest, (b) artifact digests, (c) reproducibility verification (double-build compare) or a documented, approved exception.
- Artifacts are published to staging upon green CI, with a separate manual promote job that verifies digests.
- Documentation exists in-repo (or linked Confluence) describing:
  - how to run workflow manually
  - how to interpret failures
  - what information to include when requesting a waiver

Links
- Epic: ENG-4821 Runtime LTS initiative
- Branching/versioning decision: ENG-4822
- Related: ENG-4832 (signing/provenance), ENG-4825 (perf gate integration)
- Internal support: INT-3302 (CI permissions/secrets)
implementation_notes:
Implemented GitHub Actions workflows:
- .github/workflows/release-branch-ci.yml
  - on: pull_request + push (branches: release/**, runtime-*-lts)
  - jobs: lint/test, scheduler-smoke, build-runtime-image, deterministic-rebuild-compare, publish-staging-artifacts
- .github/workflows/release-promote.yml
  - workflow_dispatch only
  - inputs: source_digest, target_tag
  - verifies staged digest == requested digest before retag/publish

Key details:
- Build uses pinned base images by digest and pinned toolchain versions.
- Determinism check rebuilds the runtime image twice from scratch (no layer cache) and compares resulting digests.
- Staging publication uses separate credentials from production publication, with least-privilege scope.

Waivers:
- Temporary waiver mechanism added via PR label + approval in the workflow UI for known flaky tests; waiver must link to a Linear issue for follow-up and expires after 14 days.
comments: 2025-01-23 (Sahana Iyer): Drafted workflow outline for release/* (separate from main). Biggest unknown is how strict we can be on determinism for CUDA/toolchain without exploding build times. Proposed: deterministic rebuild compare only for runtime image + manifests; kernel autotune caches disabled on LTS branch per Hiro/Noah guidance.

2025-01-27 (Connor O'Brien): +1. For LTS we should take the build-time hit rather than ship non-reproducible artifacts. Please keep promotion to prod tags manual + restricted; this is an enterprise audit requirement for Private.

2025-01-30 (Sahana Iyer): Blocked on secrets/permissions for staging registry namespace. Created INT-3302 with Infra. In the meantime, workflow publishes as CI artifacts only (no registry push) so we can land the required checks setup.

2025-02-03 (Sahana Iyer): Unblocked. Staging registry creds are in place with restricted scope. Added publish-staging job that pushes -rc.<run_number> tags and writes provenance + checksums to staging bucket. Promotion workflow is workflow_dispatch only and checks digests before retagging.

2025-02-06 (Allison Grant): Please ensure the release-branch CI emits a single summary artifact for Release Eng (links to logs + digests + commit). This helps us during incidents/pilot when we need to quickly confirm what is actually running.
2025-02-07 (Sahana Iyer): Added release-ci-summary.txt artifact (SHA, base image digest, runtime image digest, checksums URL, provenance URL, workflow run URL).

2025-02-10 (Sean Gallagher): SRE request: make scheduler smoke tests blocking on release branches; we’ve had regressions only show up under overload/backpressure. Also add rerun guidance in the job output (flake vs real regression).

2025-02-11 (Sahana Iyer): Scheduler smoke tests are now required checks for release branches. Added explicit failure classification in logs + a rerun button note. Flake tracking policy: if rerun passes, still requires a follow-up issue tagged 'ci-flake' if it happens more than once in a patch week.

2025-02-14 (Connor O'Brien): Marking done. Required checks are enforced on runtime-1.18-lts. Promotion workflow restricted to Release Eng. Next: wire perf-canary gate into the release checklist (ENG-4825) and validate in first patch RC.
